sections.h2: What is the Newport News real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
The city's own assessment history lists $1.18 per $100 of assessed value for 2025-26. The Assessor's Assessment History page shows the rate has sat at that level since 2023-24, after $1.20 in 2021-22 and 2022-23 and $1.22 from 2013-14 through 2020-21.

YearTotal assessmentRate per $100Taxes
2025-26$23,634,402,300$1.18$278,885,947.14
2024-25$22,686,862,600$1.18$267,704,978.68

On a $250,000 assessment, $1.18 per $100 works out to $2,950 a year. That is arithmetic on the posted rate, not a quote for any parcel. The city also runs a tax calculator on the Assessor's site.

sections.h2: Who handles assessment and billing in Newport News?
sections.html:
The Real Estate Assessor values each parcel, and the City Treasurer bills and collects. The Assessor's page says every parcel is assessed annually, effective the following July 1, and that City Council sets the rate.

  • Real Estate Assessor: 700 Town Center Drive, Suite 220, phone 757-926-1926, email restate@nnva.gov.
  • Treasurer: P.O. Box 975, Newport News, VA 23607, phone 757-926-8731, email treasurer@nnva.gov.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 2400 Washington Avenue, phone 757-926-8752, which also staffs the Board of Review.

Real estate tax is normally due December 5 and June 5, based on the city FAQ. Improvements made to the land can show up on a supplemental bill. Some bills combine the real estate tax with a stormwater fee, and the Treasurer's payment page tells online bankers to pay the grand total per account number.

sections.h2: How does a Newport News assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Newport News uses a Board of Review that sits between September 1 and November 30 each year. Its city page says applications are accepted from July 1 through September 1, with no extensions.

  • Deadline: if September 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.
  • Late filings: an application postmarked or hand delivered after the deadline is not accepted.
  • Mail warning: the page notes that since December 24, 2025, a USPS postmark reflects the processing date, which can be later than the day you mailed.
  • Who sits on it: the Newport News Circuit Court judges appoint the Board each year.
  • Where to ask: the Board's administrative assistant at 757-812-7816.

Separate forms exist for residential and commercial appeals. The same page links a procedures document for the 2026 cycle and a letter of authorization for agents.

sections.h2: Where is Newport News, and what does the geography mean for a house?
sections.html:
Newport News sits at the southeastern end of the Virginia Peninsula, on the north shore of the James River where it meets Hampton Roads. Wikipedia lists 119.63 square miles in total, of which 69.00 are land and 50.63 are water, and an elevation of 15 feet.

The 2020 census counted 186,247 residents. The city was settled in 1691 and incorporated in 1896, and in 1958 voters in Warwick and Newport News chose to consolidate under the Newport News name. Several neighborhoods sit in what used to be the City of Warwick, so an address can have a different history than a neighbor a few miles away.

Climate is humid subtropical, with snowfall averaging 5.8 inches a season according to the same article. With 42 percent of the city's area made up of water, a seller should expect buyers to ask whether a house is near a creek, a river inlet or a mapped flood zone.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and employers shape the Newport News market?
sections.html:
Newport News has dozens of named neighborhoods, from the planned community of Hilton Village in the south to Denbigh in the north. Wikipedia also lists Oyster Point, City Center, Port Warwick, Lee Hall, Riverside, Menchville, Windsor Great Park and the East End, among others. Port Warwick and City Center at Oyster Point came from New Urbanism projects that began in the early 2000s.

Employment is tied to the water and the military. The article gives these figures for the largest employers:

  • Newport News Shipbuilding, owned by Huntington Ingalls Industries: over 24,000 employees.
  • Fort Eustis: over 10,000.
  • Newport News School System: over 5,000.
  • Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility: over 675 staff.

Interstates 64 and 664 and the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel connect the city to the rest of Hampton Roads, and Newport News/Williamsburg International Airport is inside city limits.

sections.h2: What does the city's assessment ratio and tax base tell a seller?
sections.html:
The assessment history shows a 100 percent ratio every year, which means the city assesses at full value and applies the rate to that figure. Total taxable assessment for 2025-26 is $23,634,402,300, about 4.2 percent above the $22,686,862,600 listed for 2024-25.

The Assessor's page describes the work in plain terms: assess all real estate, administer the laws on assessments and exemptions, keep records on every parcel, publish an annual land book and review assessments with owners. If your value jumped, ask for that review before the September 1 appeal deadline arrives.

The Assessor does not set the rate or assessment policy. The FAQ says the rate comes from City Council and the tax equals assessed value times the rate, so a disagreement about the dollar amount is a conversation with Council, while a disagreement about value is an appeal.

sections.h2: What happens to tax owed when a Newport News house is sold?
sections.html:
Virginia law puts a tax lien on the real estate ahead of any other lien, so delinquent tax gets paid from the sale proceeds. Va. Code 58.1-3340 says the buyer, or the trustee at a foreclosure sale, must apply proceeds to taxes and levies, including penalties and interest, and the treasurer then releases the lien.

The statute says the seller's liability for the year is prorated by contract, so the sale agreement should say who pays the current half. Va. Code 58.1-802 adds a state and local grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of price, paid by the seller unless the parties arrange otherwise. The circuit court clerk collects it at recording.

The Treasurer also maintains a page for real estate auctions of properties with delinquent taxes or liens, and it posts the legal notice and auction flyer. An owner who sees a notice for their own parcel has little time left to choose the terms of a sale.

sections.h2: Are there relief programs for Newport News owners behind on tax?
sections.html:
Newport News lists several relief programs, and the Commissioner of the Revenue administers them. The city's search results show pages for a real estate tax deferral for the elderly and disabled, an exemption for disabled veterans and mobile home deferral and exemption programs.

It also lists a Residential Rehabilitation Property Tax Abatement Program with its own calculator, and a VA Deed Alert tool on the Assessor's site. Rules and income limits live on those pages, so we do not repeat them here. Call 757-926-8653 for state income and tax relief questions.

If a program does not fit and the house needs more work than you can fund, a cash sale of the property as is can clear the tax at closing instead.

faqs.q: What is the Newport News property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's assessment history lists $1.18 per $100 of assessed value for 2025-26, the same as 2024-25 and 2023-24. City Council sets the rate each year, so confirm it with the Assessor or Treasurer.

faqs.q: When are Newport News real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: They are normally due December 5 and June 5. The city's FAQ also notes that improvements to the land may be billed on a supplemental bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Newport News assessment?
faqs.a: Applications to the Board of Review are accepted July 1 through September 1, and no extensions are granted. If September 1 is a weekend or holiday, the following business day is the deadline.

faqs.q: Who is the Newport News Treasurer and how do I reach the office?
faqs.a: The city lists the Treasurer's mailing address as P.O. Box 975, Newport News, VA 23607, with the phone 757-926-8731 and the email treasurer@nnva.gov. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Newport News house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia's tax lien comes first, so the title company pays the balance from your proceeds and the treasurer releases the lien. Ask for a written payoff amount before closing.
